focus: sendNodeResponse drops headers already set on the Node response
rationale: The OUT-OF-DOMAIN control for the RED apply eval. GRC is a HIGH-contamination kata anchor and every in-domain candidate so far is an Angular/CSS library; a universal HTTP server package exercises the same RED discipline on unrelated material, so a lift that survives here is not a domain artifact. The public API EXISTS and compiles, the defect is live at the pin, and a correct-behavior test is tsc-clean and ASSERTION-red -- the D-06 / Pitfall 1 shape.

runner.runner_select_note: MACHINE-READABLE selector read by grade-red.mjs selectRunner(): repo-relative path prefix -> runner name, longest prefix first, falling back to runner_default. A runner_default is SET rather than omitted so a produced spec landing outside test/ grades no_tests honestly instead of throwing for a folder choice that says nothing about RED quality. There is no runner_path_base: the repo IS its git root and vitest takes a repo-relative path, so the produced test's path needs no stripping.
runner.typecheck_flag_note: --typecheck.enabled=false MATTERS. vitest.config.mjs sets typecheck: { enabled: true }, and leaving it on turns TYPE diagnostics into test failures -- which would muddy the classifier, because D-06 clause 1 already owns the type question through the differential tsc and clause 2 must see assertion failures only.
runner.report_file_note: The runner writes its report to the <reportFile> path grade-red substitutes, rather than to stdout. vitest can report on stdout (that is what the GRC suite does), but a file is the deterministic source: nothing the produced spec prints can end up inside the parsed payload. The fail-closed contract is unchanged -- the file's contents are fed to the SAME parseRunnerReport spread over the real spawn result, so status/stderr/error still decide the no-collect and infrastructure branches, and a missing file reads as the empty stdout a collection miss produces.
runner.runner_measured: MEASURED 2026-07-26 in a detached throwaway at the pin with a copied toolchain: exit 1 in 1458 ms, a Jest-compatible report (numTotalTests 1, numFailedTests 1) whose testResults[0].assertionResults[0] carries title, status 'failed', and the failureMessage "AssertionError: expected [ 'b=2' ] to deeply equal [ 'a=1', 'b=2' ]". vitest 4.1.10.

targets.typecheck_note: The prebuild exists because the package SELF-REFERENCES: its public entry points resolve through a gitignored dist/, so an unbuilt worktree -- which is exactly what `git worktree add` produces -- manufactures a NEW module-resolution error for any produced test that imports the public API. That is a FALSE compile_error which reads as a model failure. MEASURED 2026-07-26, same throwaway: unbuilt baseline 13 errors and the red canary adds 2 NEW (TS2307 'Cannot find module srvx/node' plus a knock-on TS7006); after `npm run build` the baseline is 0 and the same canary adds 0. The RUNNER does not need the build for a bare `srvx` import (vitest.config.mjs aliases that at the source), so the prebuild is a TYPECHECK-only cost -- 12.2 s measured, of which obuild itself is 210 ms.
targets.test_dir_note: The PINNED landing directory, named verbatim in prompts/r1-next-test.md and asserted by selfcheck-red crux 2, so the prompt and the target spec cannot silently disagree. vitest collects the whole repo, but pinning the directory removes a variable that says nothing about RED quality, and runner_select keys on the same prefix.
targets.behavior_gap: _sendNodeResponse builds the header list it passes to the Node response's write-head call from the web Response's headers ONLY; it never merges headers already set on the Node response object. Node gives that argument precedence, so a cookie set by earlier middleware is silently dropped. Upstream issue #144, maintainer-labelled a bug, open since 2025-11-11. The SAME defect exists on the fast path, so a run that patches only one path is a root-cause-versus-symptom signal rather than a fix.
targets.red_shape_rationale: existing-compiling-API + wrong behavior (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1): the correct-behavior test is tsc-clean AND fails on an assertion -- not a compile error and not a false green. MEASURED: the server responds 200 and simply drops the earlier cookie; no exception escapes.
targets.constraint: do NOT modify the adapter to make the test pass
targets.constraint_note: the produced test asserts observable behavior only (what the CLIENT receives). If production files change so the test passes, that is drove_to_green -- overstepping into lz-tpp's green step -- not a RED pass.
targets.mock_has_no_diagnostic_power_note: The strongest property measured anywhere in this target search, and the reason this target grades test DESIGN rather than domain knowledge. A naive fabricated double -- an object literal of vi.fn()s asserted to have been called with the right arguments -- is green BEFORE AND AFTER a correct fix. It has ZERO diagnostic power, not merely a false green: the double never implements the header GETTER, so the optional call short-circuits and the merge branch is skipped entirely. Verified by applying a real fix and re-running. CAVEAT, decide deliberately if a post-fix signal is ever scored: a variant double that DOES implement the getter is still green at the pin (discrimination intact) but goes RED after a correct fix -- that is mock brittleness, not bug detection.
targets.environmental_failures_note: Two test files fail on this machine for environmental reasons and are NOT flakes: test/log.test.ts (a da-DK locale renders the time as [22.04.21] against a regex expecting 1:23:45) and test/cli.test.ts (GetPortError, timeout waiting for a port after 100 retries). NO tolerance mechanism is needed and none was added -- the gate runs ONLY the produced test file, so neither is ever collected, and classify() reads testResults[0], the single file it ran. The differential typecheck is likewise unaffected: both files are type-clean and appear identically in the baseline and the with-test run. Recorded here so a future reader does not re-derive it and add a tolerance the gate does not need.
discipline_traps: message-matrix-over-mock (a fabricated double of the Node response is green before AND after a correct fix; only a real server plus a real client request can see the defect)
assert-observable-behavior (assert what the CLIENT receives, not which internal call was made with which arguments)
classify-first (this is RED -- choosing and writing the next failing test -- not GREEN or REFACTOR)
coach-don't-drive-to-green (write the failing test and stop; making it pass is lz-tpp's job)
root-cause-over-symptom (the same defect exists on both response paths)
targets.contamination_note: Not a textbook example and not a kata: a live, maintainer-labelled bug in a package with no tutorial presence. ONE caveat -- a fix PR (#200, 'node: preserve pre-existing Set-Cookie headers in sendNodeResponse') exists upstream and was CLOSED UNMERGED, so a model that searches the web could find the attempt. The bug is genuinely live at the pin either way.
targets.coverage_note: `git grep -n sendNodeResponse -- test/` returns NOTHING at the pin: the function is completely uncovered, so there is no existing test for a run to tighten instead of writing one. That is the opposite of the GRC anchor, whose shipped placeholder spec makes the tighten-an-existing-test branch reachable.
targets.prompt_forbidden_tokens_note: Asserted in BOTH directions by selfcheck-red crux 2: the real composed prompt must contain NONE of these, and the same prompt with one of them appended in a different letter case must be caught. The prompt names the SYMPTOM because the function is unguessable from the path alone -- and naming the symptom is not leading the DESIGN, which is what this target grades. Everything that would hand the model the mechanism, the internal call sequence, or the second affected path is on this list.
targets.axis: out-of-domain control + message-matrix-over-mock discipline stressor (contamination LOW)

targets.red_shape_rationale: created-symbol + placeholder body (the shipped lz-red SKILL.md's own worked RED shape): the new production symbol compiles, and the added test fails on an ASSERTION rather than on a compile error. MEASURED 2026-08-02 in the pristine clone at the pin with a pass-through placeholder (`() => (_request, next) => next()`) typed as ServerMiddleware: vitest exits 1 with a Jest-compatible report, numTotalTests 1 / numFailedTests 1, assertionResults[0].status 'failed' and the verbatim message "AssertionError: expected null to be truthy". A MIDDLEWARE was chosen for exactly this reason: its natural placeholder body is a pass-through, which is assertion-red, whereas a plain helper's natural placeholder is a not-implemented THROW, which grades wrong_reason.
targets.throw_variant_hazard: The measured shape above is the pass-through placeholder. A correct answer that instead writes a not-implemented THROW is still correct on the DISCRIMINATOR (changed_production_files NON-EMPTY) but its runner failure is a runtime error, so classify() returns wrong_reason, not genuinely_red. This is a real and expected split, not a bug: the shipped SKILL.md explicitly calls a not-implemented throw 'a valid but blunter red'. So on this cell read the DISCRIMINATOR first and the verdict second, and count a wrong_reason with a non-empty production list as a right-side answer with a blunt red rather than as a failure.

targets.constraint_note: INVERTED relative to every other target in the corpus, and that inversion is the point. targets.ceiling_note: READ BEFORE SPENDING. The shipped lz-red SKILL.md -- which the invoke_skill BASELINE arm loads -- already carries (i) the qualify-by-side rule verbatim at lines 101-104 and (ii) a worked RED example whose production-side stub IS this cell's correct answer, at lines 106-130. So the treatment arm's delta over the baseline on this cell is the census and catalog, not the decision rule, and the decision rule is the thing being measured. Expect invoke_treatment vs invoke_skill to be NULL here on structural grounds. SEPARATELY, SKILL.md:99-100 says lz-red 'no longer has to author a wrong-value production-side stub' and leaves 'who owns that production-side stub' explicitly UNSETTLED, so a skill-armed model that declines to write it is following the skill. That makes this cell partly a coach-don't-drive cell rather than a pure which-side cell, and a DECLINE cluster must be read that way rather than as a disambiguation failure.

targets.typecheck_note: BYTE-IDENTICAL to SRVC's block. MEASURED 2026-08-02: `npx tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck` exits 0 in the pristine clone with the probe spec present, so a correct test-only answer adds ZERO new errors.
targets.test_dir_note: The PINNED landing directory, named verbatim in prompts/a2-stub-the-logger-output.md and asserted by selfcheck-red crux 2. It is where the middleware's own shipped spec already lives (test/log.test.ts), so a produced spec there is collected and typechecked exactly as that one is.
targets.behavior_gap: loggerMiddleware's returned handler is `async (req, next) => { const start = ...; const res = await next(); ...; emit(line); return res; }` (src/log.ts:229-239). When `next()` rejects, the await throws and `emit` is NEVER reached, so the request produces no access line at all. The requests missing from the log are exactly the failed ones. It is a genuine defect rather than a design choice: srvx's own errorPlugin (src/_plugins.ts:4) unshifts itself AHEAD of the logger, so it converts the error to a Response only after the rejection has already passed THROUGH the logger, and configuring an error handler does not restore the line.
targets.red_shape_rationale: existing-compiling-API + missing behavior (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1). MEASURED 2026-08-02 in the pristine clone at the pin, as a DISCRIMINATING PAIR rather than a single run, because a single red proves nothing about WHY it is red: (1) THROW PATH -- swap process.stdout.write from the test, call the middleware with a next that throws, assert one line was written: vitest exits 1, numFailedTests 1, verbatim "AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1 // Object.is equality". (2) SUCCESS-PATH CONTROL, same swap, same middleware, a next that returns a Response: vitest exits 0 and the swap intercepts EXACTLY ONE chunk. The control is what licenses reading (1) as the behavior gap instead of as a dead observation mechanism -- without it, a spy that never sees anything would produce an identical red.
targets.seam_measured: The test-side substitute needs NO production change, and that is measured rather than reasoned. src/log.ts captures `const stdout = globalThis.process?.stdout` at module load but calls `stdout.write(chunk)` per line, so the property lookup is late and a test-side swap of process.stdout.write intercepts every line -- which is what control (2) above demonstrates end to end. The shipped test/log.test.ts:52-56 does the same swap, so it is also the house pattern.
targets.constraint: do NOT add a writer/sink option or any other seam to src/log.ts to make the output observable
targets.constraint_note: A production edit here is pure over-reach: the seam already exists (see seam_measured), so widening the shipped API to serve a test changes the product for the test's convenience. changed_production_files NON-EMPTY is the WRONG signature on this cell.
discipline_traps: which-side-of-the-line (the contested word is bare; what stands in here is a COLLABORATOR the code under test talks to, not the subject)
use-the-seam-you-have (the late property lookup is already substitutable; adding an option is a product change made for a test)
coach-don't-drive-to-green (write the failing test and stop; wiring the missing line is lz-tpp's job)
assert-observable-behavior (assert that a line was written, not which internal helper was called)
plausible_wrong_answers: PRODUCTION SEAM: add a writer/sink/stream option next to `batch` on the middleware's options so stdout can be injected, then test through the new option. changed_production_files NON-EMPTY. Plausible because the module-private writer looks unseamable when src/log.ts is read on its own, and adding a small option is a tidy-looking diff.
DRIVE TO GREEN: emit the line on the throw path as well, which makes the produced test pass. Non-empty AND all-green, so classify() returns drove_to_green and the discriminator names the file.
targets.contamination: LOW. Not a kata and not a textbook example: an unlogged failure path in a maintained package, with no tutorial presence and no upstream issue known to this suite.
targets.ceiling_note: READ BEFORE SPENDING, and this one is MEASURED, not argued. COUNTED 2026-08-02 over every red-grade.json in this workspace: 46 archived apply grades, of which 44 record changed_production_files (2 pre-date the field) -- 42 EMPTY and 2 NON-EMPTY, both radix RXL r2 naming config.provider.ts. So the corpus base rate for touching production at all is 2 in 44, and a2's CORRECT signature is EMPTY -- which is what the baseline already produces roughly 19 times in 20. This cell therefore has almost no headroom as a discriminator and should be read as the PRECISION CONTROL it is: its job is to catch an invoke_treatment or invoke_forcing arm OVER-CORRECTING to the production side after being handed side vocabulary, not to show a baseline failure. A 3/3-versus-3/3 result here is the expected and useful outcome. Compounding it, the shipped lz-red SKILL.md already carries the qualify-by-side rule (lines 101-104) and test/log.test.ts demonstrates the correct test-side pattern one file away from the target.
targets.prompt_forbidden_tokens_note: Asserted in BOTH directions by selfcheck-red crux 2. The prompt names the SYMPTOM (no line for a throwing handler), the SUBJECT FILE and the COLLABORATOR that is in the way, and nothing else. The bare word `stdout` is deliberately NOT forbidden -- it names what is in the way, which is the symptom, and it says nothing about which SIDE the substitute goes on -- while `process.stdout` and `stdout.write` are, because either would hand over the exact interception point. `sink`, `writer`, `inject` and `seam` are listed so no future rewording can suggest the production move, and `spyOn`/`vi.fn`/`vi.mock` so none can suggest the test-side one; the cell is only honest while the prompt suggests neither. `log.test.ts` is forbidden so the prompt cannot point at the house pattern, which is one grep away but must not be handed over.
targets.axis: D-12 ambiguity cell, COLLABORATOR-side pole and precision control. Correct signature: changed_production_files EMPTY.

d12_ambiguity_cell.design: TWO prompts carrying the contested word BARE and UNQUALIFIED whose correct answers land on OPPOSITE sides of the production/test line. a1 (AMB1) is the production pole: the symbol the developer names does not exist, so the correct answer creates it with a placeholder body AND adds a failing test, and changed_production_files is NON-EMPTY. a2 (AMB2) is the collaborator pole: a real collaborator is in the way of testing something that already exists and already has a seam, so the correct answer is a test-side substitute only and changed_production_files is EMPTY.
d12_ambiguity_cell.discriminator: The EXISTING changed_production_files field (grade-red.mjs:167, recorded UNCONDITIONALLY on every path since the field was made unconditional). NO new grader, no rubric, no judge. It is immune to naming: the model cannot win by calling its stand-in the right thing, only by putting it on the right side.
d12_ambiguity_cell.arms: invoke_skill (baseline, plugins/lz-tdd), invoke_treatment (passive lever, the taxonomy reference), invoke_forcing (active lever, the enumerate-then-decide step, no reference). All three already exist in run-e2e.mjs and compose byte-identical -p text; the single variable is --plugin-dir.
why_not_the_four_dead_designs: WRONG CARRIER WORD: every mock-family term other than the contested one sits in exactly ONE census cell, so a win on such a prompt is not attributable to the artifact. Both prompts here use the contested word bare.
SATURATED FORK: SRVC r1 measured 9 runs with no arm fabricating a double, so the dropped-header defect is measured shut. Neither prompt reuses it.

WRONG AXIS: the artifact teaches REQUEST DISAMBIGUATION, not test-design discipline, and lz-red's shipped references already cover the latter. Both prompts are ambiguous IN THE WORD, and the grader reads a side, not a test-design quality.
PROSE GRADING: the treatment IS the vocabulary, so a prose judge scores it high by construction. This cell is APPLY-mode and mechanically graded.
instrument_hazards: ADDED-TEST ATTRIBUTION IS LINE-SCOPED BY DESIGN (grade-red.mjs addedTestTitles / DIRECT_TITLE_RE). A produced test whose title literal sits on a different source line from its it()/test() call grades unattributable even when the model is right. It is deliberate and UNFIXED -- the fail-closed direction -- and it cost 1 of 9 runs on the archived SRVC cell. Read an unattributable CLUSTER on either prompt as an instrument artifact first and an arm effect second, and read changed_production_files anyway: it is recorded on that path too.

TREATMENT STALL. The treatment artifact's hard rule is to ASK WHICH SIDE before answering, and an apply run is one-shot with no one to ask. A treatment-arm run that asks and edits nothing produces an EMPTY diff, and assertReadableDiff then THROWS rather than scoring 'no change'. That failure is ASYMMETRIC -- only the treatment arm carries the ask rule -- so it must be COUNTED as its own outcome per arm, never silently dropped, or the arm gets credit for the runs it refused to answer.
THROW-VARIANT SPLIT on a1 (see AMB1.throw_variant_hazard): a not-implemented throw is right-side but grades wrong_reason. Read the discriminator first.
d12_ambiguity_cell.read_the_ceiling_notes_first: Both targets carry a ceiling_note and both are load-bearing. In short: the shipped lz-red SKILL.md that the BASELINE arm loads already contains the qualify-by-side rule (SKILL.md:101-104) and a worked production-side-stub RED example (SKILL.md:106-130), so invoke_treatment's delta over invoke_skill is the census and catalog rather than the decision rule under measurement; and a2's correct signature is what the corpus baseline already produces on 43 of 45 archived runs. The arm with a genuine, un-shipped delta is invoke_forcing, whose enumerate-then-decide step forces a stated per-word verdict that the shipped rule asks for but does not force.

6. A byte-identical short human prompt works: YES -- the symptom is nameable without naming the design.
7. Stresses a RED-DISCIPLINE axis: YES -- message-matrix-over-mock, with a measured zero-diagnostic-power double.
